cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Could You Just…
cards.instruction: Turn a difficult task into tiny favors until the help quietly becomes most of the task.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Could you hold this shelf bracket against the holes? It keeps slipping.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Could you turn that top screw once? Then you can let go.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's holding. The other screws are already lined up.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Just tighten those, then? And slide the shelf onto it to check. I'll get your coat.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 and A3 announce command, but A5 small-favor request and coat help do not sustain approval over the growing task.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 limited availability causes A3 one-turn release promise; B4 aligned screws causes A5 further installation, while the restriction answers no question.

relationship.evidence: B2 has work clothing and time pressure; B4 reports progress, credibly helping rather than simply resisting.

heightening.evidence: B4 first success becomes A5 most remaining installation under the label of checking.

specificity.evidence: A1 bracket slipping and B2 departure constraint establish a concrete difficult task and limited favor.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 getting the coat while B finishes is earned by the time limit, but A3 generic authority phrase breaks the quiet accumulation.
